subject: SIG evidence: access control runbooks, screenshots, and Drive artifacts
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <security@acme.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: access control artifacts needed

Hi Diego,

Thanks for taking SIG questions earlier. We are running the evidence collection for Acme's vendor assessment and need a couple of items to complete the Access Control matrix:

1) A runbook or operational procedure that describes how Redwood handles privilege escalation requests and emergency access (on-call runbook, approval flow).
2) Screenshots showing the GCP IAM project roles or equivalent (labels redacted as needed).
3) Any diagram that shows where KMS/HSM keys are used for tenant data encryption in transit and at rest.

Can you either attach these or share a Drive folder with view-only links (we will not request edit access)? Our deadline for this packet is Friday 2027-10-08.

Thanks,
Jordan
Security Engineer, Acme Industries
From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <security@acme.com>, sig-requests@acme.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-01T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access control artifacts needed

Jordan,

Appreciate the clear list. I'll assemble the runbook and the diagrams — I can share a Drive folder with read-only links. Quick notes:

- For screenshots we typically redact project ids and customer names; if you need full-resolution artifacts under an NDA we can escalate.
- Karthik (cc'd) will validate the runbook steps for emergency access and ensure the on-call rotation snippet is included.

I'll aim to post the folder by EOD Oct 2. If there are any additional file-format preferences (PDF vs docx) let me know.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-01T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access control artifacts needed

Diego —

I'll review and sign off on the runbook wording (privilege escalation & emergency access). Mina will pull the GCP IAM screenshot set and redact project ids. A couple of internal reminders for the runbook: include the ticketing ID pattern required for emergency approval, and the safelist IP ranges for VPN jump host. I'll add a short appendix on KMS usage with the diagram that Ops maintains.

Karthik
Director, Platform Security
From: mina.haddad@redwood.com
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-02T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access control artifacts needed

Diego / Karthik —

I've uploaded the artifacts to a share folder and set it to view-only for acme's domain. Contents:
- 2027-10-02_access_control_runbook.pdf (includes escalation flow, on-call rota, approval SLAs)
- gcp_iam_screenshots_redacted.zip (screenshots of role bindings; project ids redacted with overlay)
- kms_keyflow_network_diagram.png (high-level diagram showing where customer data is encrypted and where KMS calls occur)

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_SIG_Acme_Access_Runbooks

Notes: the runbook references our internal ticket prefix "OPS-"; I replaced a live ticket number with OPS-XXXX for the public copy. If Acme requests original filenames for audit, we should redact only the customer-unique identifiers, not operational timestamps.

Mina
Site Reliability Engineer
From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <security@acme.com>, sig-requests@acme.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-02T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access control artifacts needed

Jordan —

Drive folder shared: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_SIG_Acme_Access_Runbooks
Files included (public copy):
- 2027-10-02_access_control_runbook.pdf (privilege escalation & emergency access runbook)
- gcp_iam_screenshots_redacted.zip (role binding screenshots, redacted)
- kms_keyflow_network_diagram.png (high-level KMS usage diagram)

We set viewer permissions limited to acme domain. If you don't see access, let me know the exact email addresses and I'll add them. Karthik and Mina are on cc if you have technical questions about any artifact.

Action items for Acme: confirm the runbook version and whether the redactions meet audit requirements (we can provide a redacted checklist).

Thanks,
Diego
From: Jordan Lee <security@acme.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: sig-requests@acme.com
Date: 2027-10-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: access control artifacts needed

Diego —

Received the Drive link and reviewed the runbook and screenshots briefly. A few follow-ups before we close the packet:

1) Can you include one screenshot that shows the role binding audit log entry (timestamp + role change) — redacted is fine, we need to see the audit trail exists.
2) For the KMS diagram: could you add a short caption indicating whether keys are customer-specific (per-tenant) or global? We need that called out in the Access Control matrix.
3) Please attach the runbook PDF as an attachment to this thread (so auditors have a copy in the request ticket).

If you can get these by end of day Oct 5 we'll be set for our internal review. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Jordan
(Attachment stub: access_control_runbook.pdf — 480KB, PDF)
